panels.title: Service Map
panels.description: One edge per workload pair over the dashboard's time range, weighted by total bytes sent. Pod names are reduced to their workload by stripping the generated suffix, so a Deployment with many pods is one node. Endpoints the resolver could not name collapse to one node per kind (unresolved-raw, unresolved-host) instead of vanishing, and are usually among the highest-degree nodes here — that is external traffic with no Kubernetes object behind it, not a gap in the query.

targets.expr: label_join(sum by (source, target) (label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(label_join(label_join(sum by (src_k8s_name, dst_k8s_name, src_k8s_kind, dst_k8s_kind) (sum_over_time(sent_raw{otel_scope_name=~"$scope"}[$__range])), "dst_node", ":", "dst_k8s_name", "dst_k8s_kind"), "src_node", ":", "src_k8s_name", "src_k8s_kind"), "src_node", "$1$2", "src_node", "^(.+?)(?:-[a-z0-9]{5,}-[a-z0-9]{5,}|-[a-z0-9]{5}|-[0-9]+)(:pod)$"), "dst_node", "$1$2", "dst_node", "^(.+?)(?:-[a-z0-9]{5,}-[a-z0-9]{5,}|-[a-z0-9]{5}|-[0-9]+)(:pod)$"), "source", "$1", "src_node", "^([^:]+):.+$"), "target", "$1", "dst_node", "^([^:]+):.+$"), "source", "unresolved-$1", "src_node", "^:(.+)$"), "target", "unresolved-$1", "dst_node", "^:(.+)$")), "id", " -> ", "source", "target") > 0

title: Service Map
description: Service map from Inspektor Gadget's top_tcp collector. sent_raw and received_raw are per-interval DELTAS: the gadget drains its eBPF map on every fetch, so each sample is the bytes moved in roughly one second. avg_over_time(...[$__interval]) is therefore already a rate in bytes/second, and rate() must not be used — these are gauges. A quiet link produces no datapoint and goes stale rather than holding its last value, so a gap means no traffic, not a failed scrape. Identity is pod-level (kubeipresolver does not walk owner references), so the node graph strips the generated pod suffix to get workload nodes, and roughly half the endpoints are unresolved — kind raw or host with an empty name — so they collapse into one node per kind and stay visible in the graph rather than being dropped. There is no service label on these series: the gadget exporter emits no k8s.pod.* resource attributes, so otelcol's k8s_attributes processor cannot associate them and transform/service never fires. Filter on otel_scope_name, not service.
